modelEssay.title: Help others, and you will be helped when you are in need
modelEssay.content:
The saying 'Help others, and you will be helped when you are in need' resonates with the timeless principle of reciprocity. It suggests that when we extend a helping hand to others, we are sowing seeds of goodwill that will one day bear fruit when we ourselves require assistance.

In our daily lives, numerous instances validate this adage. For instance, during the COVID-19 pandemic, communities around the world rallied together to support healthcare workers and the elderly, providing food and essential supplies. In return, these communities were bolstered by global support and resources when they faced their own crises. Moreover, helping others not only fosters a sense of community and unity but also instills a profound sense of personal fulfillment and happiness. Acts of kindness, no matter how small, can create a ripple effect, inspiring others to pay it forward.

In conclusion, the wisdom of this saying is evident in its universal application. It reminds us that the act of helping others is not just a one-way street; it is a cycle that enriches our lives and strengthens the fabric of society.

transcript.text: Conversation 1.
transcript.translation: 对话1。

transcript.text: And now, for the lighter side of the news, Europe is setting an example for the rest of the world when it comes to food waste.
transcript.speaker: M
transcript.translation: 现在，转到新闻的轻松一面，欧洲在食物浪费方面为世界其他地区树立了榜样。

transcript.text: That's right, John.
transcript.speaker: F
transcript.translation: 没错，约翰。

transcript.text: This week, the Italian government passed legislation that aimed to dramatically reduce the amount of food wasted in the country.
transcript.speaker: F
transcript.translation: 本周，意大利政府通过了旨在大幅减少该国食物浪费的立法。

transcript.text: New laws have been put into place that will make it easier for farms and supermarkets to donate unsold foods to those who are in need.
transcript.speaker: F
transcript.translation: 新法律已经实施，这将使农场和超市更容易将未售出的食物捐赠给有需要的人。

transcript.text: Yes, and in addition to this, businesses will now be rewarded for successful efforts to cut food waste.
transcript.speaker: M
transcript.translation: 是的，除此之外，企业现在将因成功减少食物浪费的努力而获得奖励。

transcript.text: Italy is not the only country to focus on reducing food waste.
transcript.speaker: M
transcript.translation: 意大利并不是唯一关注减少食物浪费的国家。

transcript.text: Just earlier this year, the European Parliament voted in favour of legislation that would stop grocery giants from unfair trading practices that result in overproduction, thus creating waste.
transcript.speaker: M
transcript.translation: 就在今年早些时候，欧洲议会投票支持了一项立法，该立法将阻止食品巨头进行导致生产过剩从而产生浪费的不公平贸易行为。

transcript.text: In France, the government has banned supermarkets from throwing away edible foods and imposed harsh penalties on businesses that fail to comply with the regulations.
transcript.speaker: F
transcript.translation: 在法国，政府已禁止超市丢弃可食用食品，并对不遵守规定的企业施加严厉处罚。

transcript.text: While there is still much progress to be made, other countries could learn a thing or two from the example set by France and Italy.
transcript.speaker: F
transcript.translation: 尽管仍有很大进步空间，其他国家可以从法国和意大利树立的榜样中学到一两件事。

transcript.text: In the United States, up to 40% of all food goes uneaten, despite the fact that one in seven American households lacks regular access to good food.
transcript.speaker: M
transcript.translation: 在美国，高达40%的食物未被食用，尽管每七个美国家庭中就有一个缺乏定期获取优质食物的途径。

transcript.text: One major cause of this problem is the confusion over food expiration labels, which are currently not regulated by the government.
transcript.speaker: M
transcript.translation: 这个问题的一个主要原因是关于食品保质期标签的混淆，这些标签目前不受政府监管。

transcript.text: All this could change soon.
transcript.speaker: F
transcript.translation: 所有这一切可能很快就会改变。

transcript.text: This wave of new laws in Europe will definitely put more pressure on lawmakers to reduce food waste here.
transcript.speaker: F
transcript.translation: 欧洲的这波新法律无疑将给立法者带来更多压力，以减少这里的食物浪费。

transcript.text: We turn now to a spokesperson from Harvard University's Food Law and Policy Clinic for more on this story.
transcript.speaker: M
transcript.translation: 我们现在转向哈佛大学食品法律与政策诊所的发言人，了解更多关于这个故事的信息。

transcript.text: And now, let's welcome Professor Edward Baker to speak to us.
transcript.speaker: F
transcript.translation: 现在，让我们欢迎爱德华·贝克教授为我们讲话。

transcript.text: Passage 1.
transcript.translation: 短文一。

transcript.text: Barbie dolls have a particular look to them.
transcript.translation: 芭比娃娃有其独特的外观。

transcript.text: They are thin, tall, long-legged, and virtually unlike any real human being.
transcript.translation: 她们纤细、高挑、腿长，几乎不像任何真实的人类。

transcript.text: Although, over the years, Barbie has had more than 180 different careers, including football coach, sign language teacher, ambassador, president, and astronaut.
transcript.translation: 尽管多年来，芭比娃娃担任过超过180种不同的职业，包括足球教练、手语教师、大使、总统和宇航员。

transcript.text: Her body shape hasn't changed much.
transcript.translation: 她的体型变化不大。

transcript.text: Last year, Mattel, the company that makes Barbie dolls, added some Barbies to its line that have different skin tones and hair textures.
transcript.translation: 去年，制造芭比娃娃的公司美泰在其产品线中增加了一些具有不同肤色和发质的芭比娃娃。

transcript.text: There are now Barbies with one of seven skin tones, 22 eye colours, and 24 hairstyles to choose from.
transcript.translation: 现在有芭比娃娃提供七种肤色、22种眼睛颜色和24种发型可供选择。

transcript.text: Last year, Mattel also gave Barbie a flat foot, rather than forcing her to be in heels all the time like the original Barbie is.
transcript.translation: 去年，美泰还给芭比娃娃设计了平底脚，而不是像最初的芭比那样一直让她穿高跟鞋。

transcript.text: Now, they are introducing new Barbies with three slightly different body shapes, while the original tall and thin Barbies will continue to be sold.
transcript.translation: 现在，他们推出了三种略有不同体型的新芭比娃娃，而最初的纤细高挑芭比将继续销售。

transcript.text: In a statement on its website, the company says it wants Barbies to look more like real people, and to give girls everywhere infinitely more ways to spark their imagination and play out their stories.
transcript.translation: 公司在其网站上的一份声明中表示，希望芭比娃娃看起来更像真人，并为各地女孩提供更多方式来激发想象力和演绎她们的故事。

transcript.text: Although many people say the new Barbies are a step in the right direction, some people say they don't go far enough.
transcript.translation: 尽管许多人说新芭比娃娃是朝着正确方向迈出的一步，但有些人说它们做得还不够。

transcript.text: They say that the new body shapes could be even more different from the original tall, thin Barbies.
transcript.translation: 他们说新的体型本可以与最初的纤细高挑芭比有更多不同。

transcript.text: Sales of Barbie dolls have been falling every year since 2012, according to CBC News.
transcript.translation: 据CBC新闻报道，自2012年以来，芭比娃娃的销量每年都在下降。

transcript.text: The toys aren't in stores yet, but they will be sold online at the Barbie website, starting this week, for $9.
transcript.translation: 这些玩具尚未在商店上架，但从本周起，将在芭比网站上在线销售，售价为9美元。

transcript.text: Passage 2.
transcript.translation: 第二段。

transcript.text: The earliest printed book we know today appeared in China in the year 868, and metal type was in use in Korea at the beginning of the 15th century.
transcript.translation: 我们今天所知的最早的印刷书籍于公元868年出现在中国，而金属活字印刷在15世纪初的韩国已经使用。

transcript.text: But it was in Germany, around the year 1450, that a printing press using movable metal type was invented.
transcript.translation: 但正是在德国，大约在1450年，发明了一种使用可移动金属活字的印刷机。

transcript.text: Capitalism turned printing from an invention into an industry.
transcript.translation: 资本主义将印刷从一项发明转变为一个产业。

transcript.text: Right from the start, book printing and publishing were organised on capitalist lines.
transcript.translation: 从一开始，书籍印刷和出版就是按照资本主义路线组织的。

transcript.text: The biggest 16th century printer, Plantain of Antwerp, had 24 printing presses and employed more than 100 workers.
transcript.translation: 16世纪最大的印刷商，安特卫普的普兰坦，拥有24台印刷机，雇佣了100多名工人。

transcript.text: Only a small fraction of the population was literate, but the production of books grew at an extraordinary speed.
transcript.translation: 只有一小部分人口识字，但书籍生产以惊人的速度增长。

transcript.text: By 1500, some 20 million volumes had already been printed.
transcript.translation: 到1500年，大约2000万卷书籍已经被印刷。

transcript.text: The immediate effect of printing was to increase the circulation of works that were already popular in a handwritten form, while less popular works went out of circulation.
transcript.translation: 印刷的直接效果是增加了那些以手写形式已经流行的作品的流通，而不太流行的作品则退出了流通。

transcript.text: Publishers were interested only in books that would sell fairly quickly in sufficient numbers to cover the costs of production and make a profit.
transcript.translation: 出版商只对那些能以足够数量快速销售、以覆盖生产成本并盈利的书籍感兴趣。

transcript.text: Thus, while printing enormously increased access to books by making cheap, high-volume production possible, it also reduced choice.
transcript.translation: 因此，虽然印刷通过使廉价、高产量的生产成为可能，极大地增加了对书籍的获取，但它也减少了选择。

transcript.text: The great cultural impact of printing was that it facilitated the growth of national languages.
transcript.translation: 印刷的重大文化影响是促进了民族语言的发展。

transcript.text: Most early books were printed in Latin, but the market for Latin was limited, and in its pursuit of larger markets, the book trade soon produced translations into the national languages, emerging at the time.
transcript.translation: 大多数早期书籍是用拉丁语印刷的，但拉丁语市场有限，在追求更大市场的过程中，图书贸易很快产生了对当时正在兴起的民族语言的翻译。

transcript.text: Printing indeed played a key role in standardizing and stabilizing these languages by fixing them in print and producing dictionaries and grammar books.

transcript.text: Kwanzaa is a cultural festival during which African Americans celebrate and reflect upon their rich heritage as the products of two worlds.
transcript.translation: 宽扎节是一个文化节庆，期间非裔美国人庆祝并反思他们作为两个世界产物的丰富遗产。

transcript.text: It begins December 26th and lasts for seven days.
transcript.translation: 它始于12月26日，持续七天。

transcript.text: Kwanzaa was founded in 1966 by Dr.
transcript.translation: 宽扎节由博士于1966年创立。

transcript.text: Karenga, a college professor and African American leader, who believed that a special holiday could help African Americans meet their goals of building strong families, learning about their history, and creating a sense of unity.
transcript.translation: 卡伦加，一位大学教授和非裔美国人领袖，他认为一个特别的节日可以帮助非裔美国人实现他们的目标，即建立稳固的家庭、学习他们的历史并创造团结感。

transcript.text: After conducting extensive research in which he studied the festivals of many African groups of people, he decided that the new holiday should be a harvest or first fruits celebration, incorporating ideas from many different harvest traditions.
transcript.translation: 在进行了广泛研究，学习了许多非洲族群的节庆之后，他决定新节日应是一个丰收或初果庆典，融入了许多不同丰收传统的理念。

transcript.text: Kwanzaa is a Kiswahili word meaning the first fruits of the harvest.
transcript.translation: 宽扎节是一个基斯瓦希里语单词，意为丰收的初果。

transcript.text: The East African language of Kiswahili was chosen as the official language of Kwanzaa because it is a non-tribal language spoken by a large portion of the African population.
transcript.translation: 东非语言基斯瓦希里语被选为宽扎节的官方语言，因为它是一种非部落语言，由大部分非洲人口使用。

transcript.text: Also, its pronunciation is easy.
transcript.translation: 此外，它的发音简单。

transcript.text: Kwanzaa is based on seven principles which are unity, self-determination, collective work and responsibility, cooperative economics, purpose, creativity, and faith.
transcript.translation: 宽扎节基于七个原则，即团结、自决、集体工作和责任、合作经济、目的、创造力和信仰。

transcript.text: One principle is highlighted each day of the holiday.
transcript.translation: 节日的每一天都突出一个原则。

transcript.text: In preparation for the celebration, a straw mat is placed on the table, along with a candle holder with seven candles, one black, three red, and three green.
transcript.translation: 为庆祝做准备，在桌子上放一个草席，旁边是一个有七支蜡烛的烛台，一支黑色、三支红色和三支绿色。

transcript.text: The black candle represents the African American people, the red is for their struggles, and the green represents their hopes for the future.
transcript.translation: 黑色蜡烛代表非裔美国人，红色代表他们的斗争，绿色代表他们对未来的希望。

transcript.text: Other items placed on the table are a variety of fruit, ears of corns, gifts, and a communal unity cup for pouring and sharing drinks.
transcript.translation: 放在桌子上的其他物品有各种水果、玉米穗、礼物和一个用于倒酒和共享饮料的公共团结杯。

transcript.text: Each day of Kwanzaa, usually before the evening meal, family and friends gather around the table and someone lights a candle, beginning with the black.
transcript.translation: 宽扎节的每一天，通常在晚餐前，家人和朋友围坐在桌旁，有人点燃蜡烛，从黑色蜡烛开始。

transcript.text: After that, candles are lit alternately from left to right.
transcript.translation: 之后，蜡烛从左到右交替点燃。

transcript.text: While the candle is being lit, a principle is recited, then each person present takes a turn to speak about the importance that principle has to himself or herself.
transcript.translation: 在点燃蜡烛时，背诵一个原则，然后在场每个人轮流谈论该原则对自己或她自己的重要性。

transcript.text: Next, the ceremony focuses on remembering those who have died.
transcript.translation: 接下来，仪式聚焦于纪念逝者。

transcript.text: A selected person pours water or juice from the unity cup into a bowl.
transcript.translation: 一个被选中的人从团结杯中将水或果汁倒入碗中。

transcript.text: That person then drinks from the cup and raises it high, saying Harambee, which means let's all pour together.
transcript.translation: 然后那个人从杯子中喝一口，并高高举起，说'哈兰比'，意思是让我们一起倒。

transcript.text: All repeat Harambee seven times, and each person drinks from the cup.
transcript.translation: 所有人重复'哈兰比'七次，每个人都从杯子中喝一口。

transcript.text: Then, names of African American leaders and heroes are called out, and everyone reflects upon the great things these people did.
transcript.translation: 然后，喊出非裔美国人领袖和英雄的名字，每个人反思这些人所做的伟大事情。

transcript.text: The ceremony is followed by a meal, and then singing and perhaps listening to African music.
transcript.translation: 仪式之后是餐食，然后是唱歌，或许还听非洲音乐。

transcript.text: The Mediterranean diet is based upon the eating patterns of traditional cultures in the Mediterranean region.
transcript.translation: 地中海饮食是基于地中海地区传统文化的饮食模式。

transcript.text: Several noted nutritionists and research projects have concluded that this diet is one of the most healthful in the world in terms of preventing such illnesses as heart disease and cancer, and increasing life expectancy.
transcript.translation: 几位著名营养学家和研究项目得出结论，这种饮食在预防心脏病和癌症等疾病以及提高预期寿命方面，是世界上最健康的饮食之一。

transcript.text: The countries that have inspired the Mediterranean diet all surround the Mediterranean Sea.
transcript.translation: 启发了地中海饮食的国家都环绕地中海。

transcript.text: These cultures have eating habits that developed over thousands of years.
transcript.translation: 这些文化拥有发展了数千年的饮食习惯。

transcript.text: In Europe, parts of Italy, Greece, Portugal, Spain, and southern France adhere to principles of the Mediterranean diet, as do Morocco and Tunisia in North Africa.
transcript.translation: 在欧洲，意大利、希腊、葡萄牙、西班牙和法国南部的部分地区遵循地中海饮食的原则，北非的摩洛哥和突尼斯也是如此。

transcript.text: Parts of the Balkan region and Turkey follow the diet, as well as Middle Eastern countries like Lebanon and Syria.
transcript.translation: 巴尔干地区和土耳其的部分地区也遵循这种饮食，中东国家如黎巴嫩和叙利亚也是如此。

transcript.text: The Mediterranean region is warm and sunny, and produces large supplies of fresh fruits and vegetables almost year-round that people eat many times a day.
transcript.translation: 地中海地区温暖阳光充足，几乎全年都能生产大量新鲜水果和蔬菜，人们每天多次食用。

transcript.text: Wine, bread, olive oil, and nuts are other staples of the region, and the Mediterranean Sea has historically yielded abundant quantities of fish.
transcript.translation: 葡萄酒、面包、橄榄油和坚果是该地区的其他主食，地中海历史上盛产丰富的鱼类。

transcript.text: International interest in the therapeutic qualities of the Mediterranean diet began back in the late 1950s, when medical researchers started to link the occurrence of heart disease with diet.
transcript.translation: 国际上对地中海饮食治疗特性的兴趣始于20世纪50年代末，当时医学研究人员开始将心脏病的发生与饮食联系起来。

transcript.text: Dr.
transcript.translation: 博士

transcript.text: Ancel Keys performed an epidemiological analysis of diets around the world.
transcript.translation: 安塞尔·凯斯对世界各地的饮食进行了流行病学分析。

transcript.text: Entitled The Seven-Country Study, it is considered one of the greatest studies of its kind ever performed.
transcript.translation: 这项名为《七国研究》的研究被认为是同类研究中最伟大的之一。

transcript.text: In it, Keys gathered data on heart disease and its potential causes from nearly 13,000 men in Greece, Italy, Croatia, Serbia, Japan, Finland, the Netherlands, and the United States.
transcript.translation: 在研究中，凯斯从希腊、意大利、克罗地亚、塞尔维亚、日本、芬兰、荷兰和美国的近13,000名男性中收集了心脏病及其潜在原因的数据。

transcript.text: The study was conducted over a period of decades.
transcript.translation: 这项研究持续了数十年。

transcript.text: It concluded that the Mediterranean people in the study enjoyed some significant health advantages.
transcript.translation: 研究得出结论，参与研究的地中海人群享有显著的健康优势。

transcript.text: The Mediterranean groups had lower mortality rates in all age brackets and from all causes, particularly from heart disease.
transcript.translation: 地中海组在所有年龄段和所有原因（尤其是心脏病）的死亡率都较低。

transcript.text: The study also showed that the Mediterranean diet is as high or higher in fat than other diets, obtaining up to 40% of all its calories from fat.
transcript.translation: 研究还表明，地中海饮食的脂肪含量与其他饮食相当或更高，高达40%的热量来自脂肪。

transcript.text: It has, however, different patterns of fat intake.
transcript.translation: 然而，它的脂肪摄入模式不同。

transcript.text: Mediterranean cooking uses smaller amounts of saturated fat and higher amounts of unsaturated fat, mostly in the form of olive oil.
transcript.translation: 地中海烹饪使用较少的饱和脂肪和较多的不饱和脂肪，主要以橄榄油的形式。

transcript.text: Saturated fats are fats that are found principally in meat and dairy products, although some nuts and vegetable oils also contain them.
transcript.translation: 饱和脂肪主要存在于肉类和乳制品中，但一些坚果和植物油也含有它们。

transcript.text: Saturated fats are used by the body to make cholesterol, and high levels of cholesterol have since been directly related to heart disease.
transcript.translation: 饱和脂肪被身体用于制造胆固醇，高水平的胆固醇与心脏病直接相关。

questionGroups.title: Apple's Stance Highlights a More Confrontational Tech Industry

material.title: Apple's Stance Highlights a More Confrontational Tech Industry

paragraphs.text: The battle between Apple and law enforcement officials over unlocking a terrorist's smartphone is the culmination of a slow turning of the tables between the technology industry and the United States government.
paragraphs.translation: 苹果公司与执法官员之间关于解锁恐怖分子智能手机的斗争，是科技行业与美国政府之间缓慢扭转局势的高潮。

paragraphs.text: After revelations by the former National Security Agency contractor Edward J. Snowden in 2013 that the government both cozied up to (讨好) certain tech companies and hacked into others to gain access to private data on an enormous scale, tech giants began to recognize the United States government as a hostile actor. But if the confrontation has crystallized in this latest battle, it may already be heading toward a predictable conclusion: In the long run, the tech companies are destined to emerge victorious.
paragraphs.translation: 在2013年，前国家安全局承包商爱德华·J·斯诺登揭露政府既讨好某些科技公司又入侵其他公司以大规模获取私人数据后，科技巨头开始将美国政府视为敌对行动者。但如果对峙在这场最新斗争中变得清晰，它可能已朝着一个可预见的结论发展：长远来看，科技公司注定会获胜。

paragraphs.text: It may not seem that way at the moment. On the one side, you have the United States government's mighty legal and security apparatus fighting for data of the most sympathetic sort: the secrets buried in a dead mass murderer's phone. The action stems from a federal court order issued on Tuesday requiring Apple to help the Federal Bureau of Investigation (F.B.I) to unlock an iPhone used by one of the two attackers who killed 14 people in San Bernardino, California, in December.
paragraphs.translation: 目前可能并非如此。一方面，美国政府强大的法律和安全机构在为最具同情心的数据而战：埋藏在一名已故大规模杀人犯手机中的秘密。这一行动源于周二发布的一项联邦法院命令，要求苹果公司协助联邦调查局（F.B.I.）解锁一部iPhone，该手机由去年12月在加利福尼亚州圣贝纳迪诺杀害14人的两名袭击者之一使用。

paragraphs.text: In the other corner is the world's most valuable company, whose chief executive, Timothy D. Cook, has said he will appeal the court's order. Apple argues that it is fighting to preserve a principle that most of us who are addicted to our smartphones can defend: Weaken a single iPhone so that its contents can be viewed by the American government and you risk weakening all iPhones for any government intruder, anywhere.
paragraphs.translation: 另一方是世界上最有价值的公司，其首席执行官蒂莫西·D·库克表示将上诉法院命令。苹果公司辩称，它正在为捍卫一个我们大多数智能手机成瘾者都能支持的原则而战：削弱一部iPhone使其内容可被美国政府查看，你就冒着削弱所有iPhone的风险，让任何政府入侵者、在任何地方都能入侵。

paragraphs.text: There will probably be months of legal tussling, and it is not at all clear which side will prevail in court, nor in the battle for public opinion and legislative favor. Yet underlying all of this is a simple dynamic: Apple, Google, Facebook and other companies hold most of the cards in this confrontation. They have our data, and their businesses depend on the global public's collective belief that they will do everything they can to protect that data.
paragraphs.translation: 可能会有数月的法律争斗，目前完全不清楚哪一方会在法庭上占上风，也不清楚在争取公众舆论和立法支持的斗争中谁会胜出。然而，这一切背后是一个简单的动态：苹果、谷歌、Facebook和其他公司在这场对抗中掌握着大部分筹码。他们拥有我们的数据，他们的业务依赖于全球公众的集体信念，即他们会尽一切努力保护这些数据。

paragraphs.text: Any crack in that front could be fatal for tech companies that must operate worldwide. If Apple is forced to open up an iPhone for an American law enforcement investigation, what is to prevent it from doing so for a request from the Chinese or the Iranians? If Apple is forced to write code that lets the F.B.I. get into the Phone 5c used by Syed Rizwan Farook, the male attacker in the San Bernardino attack, who would be responsible if some hacker got hold of that code and broke into its other devices?
paragraphs.translation: 对于必须在全球运营的科技公司来说，任何防线上的裂痕都可能是致命的。如果苹果公司被迫为美国执法调查打开一部iPhone，那么有什么能阻止它为中国或伊朗的请求做同样的事？如果苹果公司被迫编写代码让F.B.I.进入赛义德·里兹万·法鲁克（圣贝纳迪诺袭击中的男性袭击者）使用的iPhone 5c，那么如果某个黑客掌握了该代码并入侵了其他设备，谁该负责？

paragraphs.text: Apple's stance on these issues emerged post-Snowden, when the company started putting in place a series of technologies that, by default, make use of encryption to limit access to people's data. More than that, Apple - and, in different ways, other tech companies, including Google, Facebook, Twitter and Microsoft - have made their opposition to the government's claims a point of corporate pride.
paragraphs.translation: 苹果公司在这些问题上的立场出现在斯诺登事件之后，当时该公司开始实施一系列技术，默认使用加密来限制对人们数据的访问。不仅如此，苹果公司——以及以不同方式的其他科技公司，包括谷歌、Facebook、Twitter和微软——都将其对政府要求的反对作为企业自豪感的体现。

paragraphs.text: Apple's emerging global brand is privacy; it has staked its corporate reputation, not to mention the investment of considerable technical and financial resources, on limiting the sort of mass surveillance that was uncovered by Mr. Snowden. So now, for many cases involving governmental intrusions into data, once-lonely privacy advocates find themselves fighting alongside the most powerful company in the world.
paragraphs.translation: 苹果公司新兴的全球品牌是隐私；它已将企业声誉，更不用说相当的技术和财务资源投资，押注在限制斯诺登先生所揭露的那种大规模监控上。因此，现在对于许多涉及政府入侵数据的案件，曾经孤独的隐私倡导者发现自己正与世界上最强大的公司并肩作战。

paragraphs.text: "A comparison point is in the 1990s battles over encryption," said Kurt Opsahl, general counsel of the Electronic Frontier Foundation, a privacy watchdog group. "Then you had a few companies involved, but not one of the largest companies in the world coming out with a lengthy and impassioned post, like we saw yesterday from Tim Cook. Its profile has really been raised."
paragraphs.translation: “一个比较点是20世纪90年代关于加密的斗争，”电子前沿基金会（一个隐私监督组织）总法律顾问库尔特·奥普萨尔说。“那时只有几家公司参与，但没有一家世界上最大的公司发表长篇激昂的帖子，就像我们昨天从蒂姆·库克那里看到的。它的形象确实得到了提升。”

paragraphs.text: Apple and other tech companies hold another ace: the technical means to keep making their devices more and more inaccessible. Note that Apple's public opposition to the government's request is itself a hindrance to mass government intrusion. And to get at the contents of a single iPhone, the government says it needs a court order and Apple's help to write new code; in earlier versions of the iPhone, ones that were created before Apple found religion on (热衷于) privacy, the F.B.I. may have been able to break into the device by itself.
paragraphs.translation: 苹果和其他科技公司还有一张王牌：不断使其设备越来越难以访问的技术手段。注意，苹果公司公开反对政府请求本身就是对大规模政府入侵的阻碍。要获取一部iPhone的内容，政府说它需要法院命令和苹果公司的帮助来编写新代码；在早期版本的iPhone中，那些在苹果公司热衷于隐私之前创建的版本，F.B.I.可能能够自行入侵设备。

paragraphs.text: You can expect that noose (束缚) to continue to tighten. Experts said that whether or not Apple loses this specific case, measures that it could put into place in the future will almost certainly be able to further limit the government's reach.
paragraphs.translation: 你可以预期这种束缚会继续收紧。专家表示，无论苹果公司是否输掉这个具体案件，它未来可能实施的措施几乎肯定能够进一步限制政府的触角。

paragraphs.text: That's not to say that the outcome of the San Bernardino case is insignificant. As Apple and several security experts have argued, an order compelling Apple to write software that gives the F.B.I. access to the iPhone in question would establish an unsettling precedent. The order essentially asks Apple to hack its own devices, and once it is in place, the precedent could be used to justify law enforcement efforts to get around encryption technologies in other investigations far removed from national security threats.
paragraphs.translation: 这并不是说圣贝纳迪诺案件的结果不重要。正如苹果公司和几位安全专家所辩称的，一项强制苹果公司编写软件让F.B.I.访问相关iPhone的命令将建立一个令人不安的先例。该命令本质上要求苹果公司入侵自己的设备，一旦实施，这个先例可能被用来为执法部门在远离国家安全威胁的其他调查中绕过加密技术的努力辩护。

paragraphs.text: Once armed with a method for gaining access to iPhones, the government could ask to use it proactively (先发制人地), before a suspected terrorist attack - leaving Apple in a bind as to whether to comply or risk an attack and suffer a public-relations nightmare. "This is a brand-new salvo in the war against encryption," Mr. Opsahl said. "We've had plenty of debates in Congress and the media over whether the government should have a backdoor, and this is an end run around that - here they come with an order to create that backdoor."
paragraphs.translation: 一旦掌握了访问iPhone的方法，政府可能会要求在涉嫌恐怖袭击之前先发制人地使用它——让苹果公司陷入两难境地：是遵守还是冒险面临袭击并遭受公关噩梦。“这是反加密战争中一个全新的攻击，”奥普萨尔先生说。“我们在国会和媒体上就政府是否应该拥有后门进行了大量辩论，而这是绕过那个辩论的做法——他们带着创建后门的命令来了。”

paragraphs.text: Yet it's worth noting that even if Apple ultimately loses this case, it has plenty of technical means to close a backdoor over time. "If they're anywhere near worth their salt as engineers, I bet they're rethinking their threat model as we speak," said Jonathan Zdziarski, a digital forensic expert who studies the iPhone and its vulnerabilities.
paragraphs.translation: 然而值得注意的是，即使苹果公司最终输掉这个案件，它也有足够的技术手段随着时间推移关闭后门。“如果他们作为工程师还算称职，我打赌他们正在重新思考他们的威胁模型，就像我们现在说的那样，”研究iPhone及其漏洞的数字取证专家乔纳森·兹齐亚尔斯基说。

paragraphs.text: One relatively simple fix, Mr. Zdziarski said, would be for Apple to modify future versions of the iPhone to require a user to enter a passcode before the phone will accept the sort of modified operating system that the F.B.I. wants Apple to create. That way, Apple could not unilaterally introduce a code that weakens the iPhone — a user would have to consent to it.
paragraphs.translation: 兹齐亚尔斯基先生说，一个相对简单的修复方法是，苹果公司修改未来版本的iPhone，要求用户在手机接受F.B.I.希望苹果创建的那种修改后的操作系统之前输入密码。这样，苹果公司就不能单方面引入削弱iPhone的代码——用户必须同意。

paragraphs.text: "Nothing is 100 percent hacker-proof," Mr. Zdziarski said, but he pointed out that the judge's order in this case required Apple to provide "reasonable security assistance" to unlock Mr. Farook's phone. If Apple alters the security model of future iPhones so that even its own engineers' "reasonable assistance" will not be able to crack a given device when compelled by the government, a precedent set in this case might lose its lasting force. In other words, even if the F.B.I. wins this case, in the long run, it loses.
paragraphs.translation: “没有什么是100%防黑客的，”兹齐亚尔斯基先生说，但他指出，本案法官的命令要求苹果公司提供“合理的安全协助”来解锁法鲁克先生的手机。如果苹果公司改变未来iPhone的安全模型，使得即使自己的工程师在政府强制下也无法破解特定设备，那么本案确立的先例可能失去其持久力。换句话说，即使F.B.I.赢得这个案件，长远来看，它输了。

questions.statementText: It is a popular belief that tech companies are committed to protecting their customers' private data.
questions.analysis: 该陈述对应段落E。段落E中提到'Apple, Google, Facebook and other companies hold most of the cards in this confrontation. They have our data, and their businesses depend on the global public's collective belief that they will do everything they can to protect that data.'（苹果、谷歌、Facebook和其他公司在这场对抗中拥有大部分筹码。他们拥有我们的数据，并且他们的业务依赖于全球公众的共同信念，即他们会尽一切努力保护这些数据。）这与陈述中的'tech companies are committed to protecting their customers' private data'（科技公司致力于保护客户的私人数据）相对应。

questions.statementText: The US government believes that its access to people's iPhones could be used to prevent terrorist attacks.
questions.analysis: 该陈述对应段落M。段落M中提到'Once armed with a method for gaining access to iPhones, the government could ask to use it proactively (先发制人地), before a suspected terrorist attack'（一旦掌握了访问iPhone的方法，政府可能会要求在涉嫌恐怖袭击之前先发制人地使用它）。这与陈述中的'access to people's iPhones could be used to prevent terrorist attacks'（接触人们的iPhone可用于防止恐怖袭击）直接对应——'before a suspected terrorist attack'即'prevent terrorist attacks'。段落C仅描述政府为破解一部凶手手机而争数据，并未涉及'预防'袭击，故应为 M。

questions.statementText: A federal court asked Apple to help the FBI access data in a terrorist's iPhone.
questions.analysis: 该陈述对应段落C。段落C中提到'The action stems from a federal court order issued on Tuesday requiring Apple to help the Federal Bureau of Investigation (F.B.I) to unlock an iPhone used by one of the two attackers who killed 14 people in San Bernardino, California, in December.'（该行动源于周二发布的联邦法院命令，要求苹果帮助联邦调查局（FBI）解锁一名在加利福尼亚州圣贝纳迪诺杀害14人的两名袭击者之一使用的iPhone。）这与陈述中的'A federal court asked Apple to help the FBI access data in a terrorist's iPhone'（一个联邦法院要求苹果帮助FBI访问一个恐怖分子的iPhone中的数据）相对应。

questions.statementText: Privacy advocates now have Apple fighting alongside them against government access to personal data.
questions.analysis: 该陈述对应段落H。段落H中提到'So now, for many cases involving governmental intrusions into data, once-lonely privacy advocates find themselves fighting alongside the most powerful company in the world.'（因此现在，在许多涉及政府侵入数据的案件中，曾经孤独的隐私倡导者发现自己与世界上最强大的公司并肩作战。）这与陈述中的'Privacy advocates now have Apple fighting alongside them against government access to personal data'（隐私倡导者现在有苹果与他们一起对抗政府获取个人数据）相对应。

questions.statementText: Snowden revealed that the American government had tried hard to access private data in a massive scale.
questions.analysis: 该陈述对应段落B。段落B中提到'After revelations by the former National Security Agency contractor Edward J. Snowden in 2013 that the government both cozied up to (讨好) certain tech companies and hacked into others to gain access to private data on an enormous scale, tech giants began to recognize the United States government as a hostile actor.'（在前国家安全局承包商爱德华·J·斯诺登于2013年披露政府既讨好某些科技公司，又黑客攻击其他公司以获取大规模私人数据后，科技巨头开始将美国政府视为敌对行为者。）这与陈述中的'Snowden revealed that the American government had tried hard to access private data in a massive scale'（斯诺登透露美国政府曾努力获取大规模私人数据）相对应。

questions.statementText: The FBI might have been able to access private data in earlier iPhones without Apple's help.
questions.analysis: 该陈述对应段落J。段落J中提到'Note that Apple's public opposition to the government's request is itself a hindrance to mass government intrusion. And to get at the contents of a single iPhone, the government says it needs a court order and Apple's help to write new code; in earlier versions of the iPhone, ones that were created before Apple found religion on (热衷于) privacy, the F.B.I. may have been able to break into the device by itself.'（注意，苹果对政府请求的公开反对本身就是对大规模政府入侵的阻碍。要获取单个iPhone的内容，政府表示需要法院命令和苹果的帮助来编写新代码；在苹果热衷于隐私之前创建的早期版本的iPhone中，FBI可能能够自行破解该设备。）这与陈述中的'The FBI might have been able to access private data in earlier iPhones without Apple's help'（FBI可能能够在没有苹果帮助的情况下访问早期iPhone中的私人数据）相对应。

questions.statementText: After the Snowden incident, Apple made clear its position to counter government intrusion into personal data by means of encryption.
questions.analysis: 该陈述对应段落G。段落G中提到'Apple's stance on these issues emerged post-Snowden, when the company started putting in place a series of technologies that, by default, make use of encryption to limit access to people's data.'（苹果在这些问题上的立场是在斯诺登之后出现的，当时公司开始实施一系列技术，这些技术默认使用加密来限制对人们数据的访问。）这与陈述中的'After the Snowden incident, Apple made clear its position to counter government intrusion into personal data by means of encryption'（斯诺登事件之后，苹果明确了其通过加密手段对抗政府侵入个人数据的立场）相对应。

questions.statementText: According to one digital expert, no iPhone can be entirely free from hacking.
questions.analysis: 该陈述对应段落P。段落P中提到'"Nothing is 100 percent hacker-proof," Mr. Zdziarski said,'（'没有什么是100%防黑客的，'Zdziarski先生说，）这与陈述中的'According to one digital expert, no iPhone can be entirely free from hacking'（根据一位数字专家的说法，没有iPhone可以完全免于黑客攻击）相对应。

questions.statementText: Timothy Cook's long web post has helped enhance Apple's image.
questions.analysis: 该陈述对应段落I。段落I中提到'Then you had a few companies involved, but not one of the largest companies in the world coming out with a lengthy and impassioned post, like we saw yesterday from Tim Cook. Its profile has really been raised.'（那时你只有几家公司参与，但没有一家世界上最大的公司发表长篇大论和充满激情的帖子，就像我们昨天从蒂姆·库克那里看到的那样。它的知名度真的提高了。）这与陈述中的'Timothy Cook's long web post has helped enhance Apple's image'（蒂莫西·库克的长篇网络帖子帮助提升了苹果的形象）相对应。

questions.statementText: Apple's CEO has decided to appeal the federal court's order to unlock a user's iPhone.
questions.analysis: 该陈述对应段落D。段落D中提到'In the other corner is the world's most valuable company, whose chief executive, Timothy D. Cook, has said he will appeal the court's order.'（在另一边是世界上最有价值的公司，其首席执行官蒂莫西·D·库克表示他将上诉法院的命令。）这与陈述中的'Apple's CEO has decided to appeal the federal court's order to unlock a user's iPhone'（苹果的首席执行官已决定上诉联邦法院解锁用户的iPhone的命令）相对应。

questionGroups.title: Passage One

paragraphs.text: At the base of a mountain in Tanzania's Gregory Rift, Lake Natron burns bright red, surrounded by the remains of animals that were unfortunate enough to fall into the salty water. Bats, swallows and more are chemically preserved in the pose in which they perished, sealed in the deposits of sodium carbonate in the water. The lake's landscape is bizarre and deadly- and made even more so by the fact that it's the place where nearly 75 percent of the world's flamingos (火烈鸟) are born.
paragraphs.translation: 在坦桑尼亚格雷戈里裂谷的一座山脚下，纳特龙湖燃烧般地呈亮红色，周围是那些不幸落入盐水中的动物残骸。蝙蝠、燕子等动物以它们死亡时的姿势被化学方式保存，封存在水中的碳酸钠沉积物里。这片湖的景观奇异而致命——更甚的是，世界上近75%的火烈鸟在这里诞生。

paragraphs.text: The water is so corrosive that it can burn the skin and eyes of unadapted animals. Flamingos, however, are the only species that actually makes life in the midst of all that death. Once every three or four years, when conditions are right, the lake is covered with the pink birds as they stop flight to breed. Three quarters of the world's flamingos fly over from other salt lakes in the Rift Valley and nest on salt- crystal islands that appear when the water is at specific level- too high and the birds can't build their nests, too low and predators can more briskly across the lake bed and attack. When the water hits the right level. The baby birds are kept safe from predators by a corrosive ditch.
paragraphs.translation: 水具有强腐蚀性，能灼伤不适应动物的皮肤和眼睛。然而，火烈鸟是唯一能在这种死亡之地中生存的物种。每三到四年，当条件合适时，湖面上会覆盖着这些粉红色的鸟，它们停飞繁殖。世界上四分之三的火烈鸟从裂谷的其他盐湖飞来，在盐晶岛上筑巢，这些岛屿在水位特定时出现——水位太高，鸟儿无法筑巢；水位太低，捕食者能更迅速地穿过湖床攻击。当水位恰到好处时，幼鸟通过腐蚀性沟渠得以免受捕食者侵害。

paragraphs.text: "Flamingos have evolved very leathery skin on their legs so they can tolerate the salt water," says David Harper, a professor at the University of Leicester. " Humans cannot, and would die if their legs were exposed for any length of time." So far this year, water levels have been too high for the flamingos to nest.
paragraphs.translation: “火烈鸟进化出了非常坚韧的皮肤在腿上，因此能耐受盐水，”莱斯特大学教授戴维·哈珀说。“人类则不行，如果腿暴露在盐水中任何一段时间就会死亡。”今年迄今为止，水位一直太高，火烈鸟无法筑巢。

paragraphs.text: Some fish, too, have had limited success vacationing at the lake as less salty lagoons (泻湖) form on the outer edges from hot springs flowing into Lake Natron. Three species of tilapia (罗非鱼) thrive there part-time. "Fish have a refuge in the streams and can expand into the lagoons when the lake is low and the lagoons are separate," Harper said. "All the lagoons join when the lake is high and fish must retreat to their stream refuges or die." Otherwise, no fish are able to survive in the naturally toxic lake.
paragraphs.translation: 一些鱼类也在这个湖中度假取得了有限的成功，因为从温泉流入纳特龙湖，在外缘形成了盐度较低的泻湖。三种罗非鱼在那里部分时间茁壮成长。“鱼类在溪流中有避难所，当湖水低、泻湖分离时，可以扩展到泻湖中，”哈珀说。“当湖水高时，所有泻湖连接，鱼类必须撤回溪流避难所，否则就会死亡。”除此之外，没有鱼类能在这种天然有毒的湖中生存。

paragraphs.text: This unique ecosystem may soon be under pressure. The Tanzanian government has once again started mining the lake for soda ash, used for making chemicals, glass and detergents. Although the planned operation will be located more than 40 miles away, drawing the soda ash in through pipelines, conservationists worry it could still upset the natural water cycle and breeding grounds. For now, though, life prevails even in a lake that kills almost everything it touches.
paragraphs.translation: 这个独特的生态系统可能很快面临压力。坦桑尼亚政府已再次开始开采该湖的纯碱，用于制造化学品、玻璃和洗涤剂。尽管计划中的作业将位于40多英里外，通过管道抽取纯碱，但环保主义者担心这仍可能扰乱自然水循环和繁殖地。不过目前，生命依然盛行于这个几乎杀死一切触碰之物的湖中。

You should decide on the best choice and mark the corresponding letter on Answer Sheet 2 with a single line through the centre.

questions.questionText: What can we learn about Lake Natron?

options.label: A
options.text: It is simply uninhabitable for most animals.

options.label: B
options.text: It remains little known to the outside world.

options.label: C
options.text: It is a breeding ground for a variety of birds.

options.label: D
options.text: It makes an ideal habitat for lots of predators.

questions.analysis: 这是一道细节理解题。根据文章第一段描述，Lake Natron的水具有极强的腐蚀性，可以烧伤未适应的动物的皮肤和眼睛，因此大多数动物都无法在此生存。选项A正确。

wrongOptions.B: 'It remains little known to the outside world'与文章内容无关，文章并未提及Lake Natron的知名度。
wrongOptions.C: 'It is a breeding ground for a variety of birds'不正确，因为文章明确指出只有火烈鸟在此繁殖。
wrongOptions.D: 'It makes an ideal habitat for lots of predators'不正确，因为文章中提到该湖对几乎所有生物都是致命的。

questions.questionText: Flamingos nest only when the lake water is at a specific level so that their babies can.

options.label: A
options.text: find safe shelter more easily.

options.label: B
options.text: grow thick feathers on their feet.

options.label: C
options.text: stay away from predators.

options.label: D
options.text: get accustomed to the salty water.

questions.analysis: 这是一道细节理解题。文章中提到，火烈鸟只在湖水达到特定水平时筑巢，这样它们的幼鸟可以远离捕食者。因此选项C正确。

wrongOptions.A: 'find safe shelter more easily'没有在文章中提及。
wrongOptions.B: 'grow thick feathers on their feet'与火烈鸟幼鸟无关，文章中提到的是火烈鸟的腿部皮肤适应了盐水。
wrongOptions.D: 'get accustomed to the salty water'与火烈鸟幼鸟无关，文章中提到的是成年火烈鸟适应盐水。

questions.questionText: Flamingos in the Rift Valley are unique in that .

options.label: A
options.text: they can move swiftly across lagoons.

options.label: B
options.text: they can survive well in salty water.

options.label: C
options.text: they breed naturally in corrosive ditches.

options.label: D
options.text: they know where and when to nest.

questions.analysis: 这是一道细节理解题。文章中提到火烈鸟的腿部皮肤非常坚韧，可以忍受盐水，这是它们在盐湖中生存的独特之处。因此选项B正确。

wrongOptions.A: 'they can move swiftly across lagoons'与文章内容无关。
wrongOptions.C: 'they breed naturally in corrosive ditches'不正确，文章中提到的是火烈鸟的幼鸟被腐蚀性水沟保护。

questions.questionText: Why can certain species of tilapia sometimes survive around Lake Natron?

options.label: A
options.text: They can take refuge in the less salty waters.

options.label: B
options.text: They can flee quickly enough from predators.

options.label: C
options.text: They can move freely from lagoon to lagoon.

options.label: D
options.text: They can stand the heat of the spring water.

questions.analysis: 这是一道细节理解题。文章中提到，某些罗非鱼物种能够在Lake Natron周围的泻湖中生存，因为这些泻湖的盐分较低。因此选项A正确。

wrongOptions.B: 'They can flee quickly enough from predators'与文章内容无关。
wrongOptions.C: 'They can move freely from lagoon to lagoon'文章中并未提及罗非鱼可以在泻湖间自由移动。
wrongOptions.D: 'They can stand the heat of the spring water'文章中提到的是泻湖由温泉形成，但并未提及罗非鱼能承受热水。

questions.questionText: What may be the consequence of the Tanzanian government's planned operation?

options.label: A
options.text: The accelerated extinction of flamingos.

options.label: B
options.text: The change of flamingos' migration route.

options.label: C
options.text: The overmining of Lake Natron's soda ash.

options.label: D
options.text: The disruption of Lake Natron's ecosystem.

questions.analysis: 这是一道推理判断题。文章最后一段提到坦桑尼亚政府计划从Lake Natron开采苏打灰，环保人士担心这可能会破坏自然水循环和繁殖地，因此选项D正确。

wrongOptions.A: 'The accelerated extinction of flamingos'文章中并未提及火烈鸟会加速灭绝。
wrongOptions.B: 'The change of flamingos' migration route'文章中并未提及火烈鸟的迁徙路线会改变。
wrongOptions.C: 'The overmining of Lake Natron's soda ash'文章中提到的是开采苏打灰，但并未提及过度开采。

questionGroups.title: Passage Two

paragraphs.text: It is the season for some frantic last-minute math across the country, employees of all stripe are counting backward in an attempt to figure out just how much paid time-off they have left in their reserves. More of them, though, will skip those calculations altogether and just power through the holidays into 2017: More than half of American workers don't use up all of their allotted vacation days each year.
paragraphs.translation: 现在全国上下都在进行一些紧张的最后一刻的计算，各行各业的员工都在倒数，试图弄清楚他们还有多少带薪假期储备。不过，更多的人会完全跳过这些计算，直接硬撑着度过假日直到2017年：超过一半的美国工人每年都没有用完他们所有的假期。

paragraphs.text: Not so long ago, people would have turned up their noses at that kind of dedication to the job. As marketing professors Silvia Bellezza, Neeru Paharia, and Anat Keinan recently explained in Harvard Business Review (HBR), leisure time was once seen as an indicator of high social status, something attainable only for those at the top. Since the middle of the 20th century, though, things have turned the opposite way these days, punishing hours at your desk, rather than days off, are seen as the mark of someone important.
paragraphs.translation: 不久前，人们还会对这种对工作的投入嗤之以鼻。正如市场营销教授 Silvia Bellezza、Neeru Paharia 和 Anat Keinan 最近在《哈佛商业评论》(HBR) 中所解释的那样，休闲时间曾经被视为高社会地位的标志，只有那些顶级人士才能获得。然而，自20世纪中叶以来，情况已经反过来了，如今，在办公桌前度过漫长的时间，而不是休假，被视为重要人物的标志。

paragraphs.text: In a series of several experiments, the researchers illustrated just how much we've come to admire busyness, or at least the appearance of it. Volunteers read two passages, one about a man who led a life of leisure and another about a man who was over-worked and over scheduled; when asked to determine which of the two had a higher social status, the majority of the participants said the latter. The same held true for people who used products that implied they were short on time: In one experiment, for example, customers of the grocery-delivery service Peapod were seen as of higher status than people who shopped at grocery stores that were equally expensive; in another, people wearing wireless headphones were considered further up on the social ladder than those wearing regular headphones, even when both were just used to listen to music.
paragraphs.translation: 在一系列实验中，研究人员展示了我们多么崇拜忙碌，或者至少是忙碌的表象。志愿者阅读两段文字，一段关于一个过着休闲生活的男人，另一段关于一个过度工作和过度安排时间的男人；当被问及哪个人社会地位更高时，大多数参与者说后者。对于那些使用暗示时间紧张的产品的人也是如此：例如，在一个实验中，使用杂货配送服务 Peapod 的顾客被认为比在同样昂贵的杂货店购物的人地位更高；在另一个实验中，佩戴无线耳机的人被认为在社会阶梯上比佩戴普通耳机的人更高，即使两者都只是用来听音乐。

paragraphs.text: In part, the authors wrote in HBR, this pattern may have to do with the way work itself has changed over the past several decades.
paragraphs.translation: 作者在 HBR 中写道，部分原因可能与工作本身在过去几十年中的变化方式有关。

paragraphs.text: We think that the shift from leisure-as-status to busyness-as-status may be linked to the development of knowledge-intensive economics. In such economies, individuals who possess the human capital characteristics that employers or clients value(e.g., competence and ambition) are expected to be in high demand and short supply on the job market. Thus, by telling others that we are busy and working all the time, we are implicitly suggesting that we are sought after, which enhances our perceived status.
paragraphs.translation: 我们认为，从“休闲即地位”到“忙碌即地位”的转变可能与知识密集型经济的发展有关。在这样的经济中，拥有雇主或客户所重视的人力资本特征（如能力和野心）的个人，预计在就业市场上需求高而供应少。因此，通过告诉别人我们很忙并且一直在工作，我们暗示自己很抢手，从而提升我们的 perceived status。

paragraphs.text: Even if you feel tempted to sacrifice your own vacation days for fake busyness, though, at least consider leaving your weekends unscheduled. It's for your own good.
paragraphs.translation: 然而，即使你感到诱惑为了虚假的忙碌而牺牲自己的假期，至少考虑让周末保持无计划。这对你自己有好处。

questions.questionText: What do most employees plan to do towards the end of the year?

options.label: A
options.text: Go for a vacation.

options.text: Set an objective for next year.

questions.questionText: How would people view dedication to work in the past?

options.label: A
options.text: They would regard it as a matter of course.

options.label: B
options.text: They would consider it a must for success.

options.label: C

options.text: The more one works, the more one feels exploited.

questions.analysis: 这是一道细节理解题。文章第三段提到'The researchers illustrated just how much we've come to admire busyness, or at least the appearance of it'，说明人们越来越欣赏忙碌，或者至少是忙碌的外表。因此，A选项'The busier one appears, the more respect one earns'是正确答案。

questions.analysis: 这是一道细节理解题。文章第四段提到'the shift from leisure-as-status to busyness-as-status may be linked to the development of knowledge-intensive economics'，说明从休闲作为地位的象征转变为忙碌作为地位的象征可能与知识密集型经济的发展有关。因此，D选项'The role of knowledge in the modern economy'是正确答案。

questionGroups.sourceText: 洞庭湖位于湖南省东北部，面积很大，但湖水很浅。洞庭湖是长江的蓄洪池，湖的大小很大程度上取决于季节变化。湖北和湖南两省因其与湖的相对位置而得名，湖北意为"湖的北边"，而湖南则为"湖的南边"。洞庭湖作为龙舟赛的发源地，在中国文化中享有盛名。据说龙舟赛始于洞庭湖东岸，为的是搜寻楚国爱国诗人屈原的遗体。龙舟赛与洞庭湖及周边的美景，每年都吸引着成千上万来自全国和世界各地的游客。

answer.modelTranslation: Dongting Lake, located in the northeastern part of Hunan Province, is vast but has shallow waters. It serves as a flood storage reservoir for the Yangtze River, with its size largely depending on seasonal changes. The provinces of Hubei and Hunan are named based on their relative positions to the lake, with Hubei meaning 'north of the lake' and Hunan meaning 'south of the lake'. As the birthplace of dragon boat racing, Dongting Lake enjoys a prestigious reputation in Chinese culture. It is said that the dragon boat races originated from the eastern shore of Dongting Lake to search for the body of the patriotic poet Qu Yuan from the Chu state. The dragon boat races and the surrounding beautiful scenery attract tens of thousands of tourists from all over the country and around the world every year.
